slides.narration: AeroGarden Bounty vs Harvest — which model should you buy?. The Sill Garden answer for a small apartment, without buying more equipment than you need.

slides.headline:
Match the setup
to your space.
slides.subhead: Light, noise, and spill risk matter more than pod count.
slides.narration: Start with usable space, daylight, and a tray that protects the rental surface. Then pick the smallest setup that still grows what you cook.

slides.headline:
Don't buy the
biggest kit first.
slides.subhead: Weak light is not a watering problem.
slides.narration: Skip the largest system until the plants prove they need it. Stretching stems usually mean more light, not more water.

slides.headline:
Start small.
Prove the routine.
slides.subhead: Start with Harvest-class (≈6 pods) for most apartments. Step up to Bounty only if you cook herbs daily and have counter depth. Skip Farm-sca
slides.narration: Our verdict: Start with Harvest-class (≈6 pods) for most apartments. Step up to Bounty only if you cook herbs daily and have counter depth. Skip Farm-scale towers unless you have floor space. Full guide on Sill Garden dot com.
